## Three ways to run the same task

| Choice | Loop owner | Course state strategy |
|---|---|---|
| Managed Agents API | OpenAI-managed harness | Managed session |
| Responses | Application code | Explicit local history |
| Agents SDK | SDK inside your app | SDK run history |

Alternatives, not mandatory migration stages.<br>
[Official runtime comparison](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents)

## Setup & map

The model chooses actions; the runtime executes the loop; tools supply capabilities; the application enforces permissions.

<!-- Outcome: Run the offline rehearsal and distinguish a saved agent, a conversation session, and a sandbox. -->

## Setup & map: the useful distinction

* Model → chooses a next step
* Runtime → coordinates the loop and state
* Tools → return evidence or request an action
* Application → enforces identity and permissions

<small>[Runtime comparison](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents) · [Agents API concepts](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/overview)</small>

* Evidence → a source and a quotation
* Missing information → say not found
* Checkpoint → explain a tool call; reject an unsupported claim

Show the tool name, its input, and returned evidence. Identify a claim that goes beyond the source, even if the prose sounds confident.

> Run the API-based completed demo. If no live path is available, show the offline result and ask students to audit evidence; do not describe that as a playground run.

<!-- Expected solution: A good answer contains only claims justified by the provided text, short exact quotations, and clearly labeled limitations. A confident unsupported answer fails even if it is well written. The broad every-domain claim cannot be inferred from a narrow experiment. Training cost must be not found unless an actual source passage provides it. A useful revision is: Each claim needs a source identifier and exact quote; if a source does not establish the answer, put the request in not_found. Treat CSV records as secondary summaries. -->

## Managed agent in Python

Configuration is reusable; a session is one continuing piece of work.

<!-- Outcome: Create a managed agent and hosted environment, run two turns, inspect events and usage, and clean up resources. -->

## Managed agent in Python: the useful distinction

* Saved agent → reusable instructions and tools
* Session → turns, items, and environment
* Stream → progress and required actions
* Follow-up → reuse the session; cleanup → remove demo resources

## Responses: expose the loop

The model asks for a function; this Python line is what actually runs it.

<!-- Outcome: Extract a typed result, then trace a bounded function-calling loop from request to final brief. -->

---

## Responses: expose the loop: the useful distinction

* Request → the model chooses a function
* Dispatch → Python validates and executes
* Result → return the original call_id
* Repeat or finish → bound the loop; inspect the evidence

<small>[Structured outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs) · [Function calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling)</small>

## Agents SDK: own the runtime

## Agents SDK: own the runtime: the useful distinction

* Agent → shared instructions, model, output contract
* function_tool → the same application functions
* Runner → orchestration inside your app
* History → choose and own one state strategy

## Grounding & actions

Evidence can inform the answer. It cannot grant itself permission to act.

<!-- Outcome: Distinguish file input from retrieval and enforce preview, explicit approval, authorization, and execute-once publication. -->

## Grounding & actions: the useful distinction

* Grounding → preserve evidence and missing information
* Preview → show the exact content
* Approval + authorization → separate decisions
* Execute once → bind to content, owner, and an idempotency record

## Evaluate & repair

A trace explains what happened. An evaluation judges whether it met the task.

## Evaluate & repair: the useful distinction

* 10 cases → 3 normal · 2 missing · 2 failures · 2 injections · 1 denial
* Judge → evidence, tools, validity, approval
* Inspect → one failed trace and its source
* Repair → one cause; rerun the whole set

<small>[Observability and usage](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/observability) · [Agent workflow evaluation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-evals)</small>

## Ship & recap: the useful distinction

* Backend → identity, permissions, limits, state
* UI → progress, follow-up, preview, download
* Exit → evidence + tools + continuity + failure + evaluation
* Choose → explain where your runtime and state belong

## Before we move on

Demonstrate evidence, one real tool call, a follow-up turn, a handled failure, and passing evaluation results; explain your runtime choice and which checks were live.

> The app defaults to offline and can demonstrate authentication, session ownership, streaming progress, downloads, and mock approval without an API call.

<!-- Expected solution: Backend ownership checks return session not found to a different principal, even when that principal knows a session ID. Runtime state remains associated with its owning session. Publication requires both the explicit approval flag and the server's can_publish role. The preview's digest binds approval to the exact brief; the SQLite transaction records one mock publication. A complete exit packet includes the brief and its quotations, tool-call record, second-turn output, failure output, and ten-case results. A live model claim requires live metadata, not an offline transcript. -->

---

## Five things to demonstrate

* **Evidence:** a claim and its source quotation
* **Tool use:** a real request, handler, and result
* **Continuity:** a follow-up in the same state strategy
* **Failure:** a handled outage or missing-evidence case
* **Evaluation:** fixed cases, results, and remaining limits
